head: 1b635c67
feature: HTTP/3 capture-backed equal-wire comparison against quic-go v0.59.0
decision: run the kernel-capture arm under CAP_NET_RAW and record directional IP/UDP accounting plus packet-size sequences
command: sudo env GO_BIN=<go1.24.7> GOMODCACHE=<user-go-module-cache> bash tools/interop/http3_quic_go.sh <netz-client> <netz-server> --bench --capture --warmup=1 --iterations=3 --streams=1 --body-bytes=1048576 --chunk-bytes=16384 --stream-window=1048576 --timeout-ms=30000
prerequisite: sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=33554432 (restored to 212992 after the gate); capture, client, and server pinned to CPUs 2, 0, and 1
artifacts: docs/evidence/http3_equal_wire_capture/2026-11-19/ (gate.log, directional logs, comparison logs, bounded DLT_RAW PCAP prefixes, capture tool copy)
conclusion: The HTTP/3 capture arm now runs on this host with CAP_NET_RAW and a 32 MiB effective packet-socket buffer. All four mixed-role captures completed with zero drops. The workloads are close but not equal-wire: netz/quic-go sender datagram ratios are 1.016 upload and 1.005 download, while the packet-size sequences differ. Timing results remain explicitly same-application-shape; this evidence removes the kernel-capture gap without claiming byte-identical wire behavior.
